title: Pigeons Learned to Read Breast Cancer Slides in 2 Weeks
subject: pigeon

scenes.text: Doctors train for years to read these slides. Pigeons needed two weeks.
At the University of Iowa, scientists taught pigeons to tell healthy breast tissue from cancerous tissue.
Day one, they scored about 50 percent. Pure guessing. By day 15, nearly 85 percent.
Their only teacher was food, for right answers.
They did nearly as well on slides they had never seen. The hardest mammogram lumps beat them, just like they challenge doctors.
And four pigeons voting together reached 99 percent.

description:
Doctors train for years to read pathology slides. Pigeons needed two weeks to reach nearly 85 percent accuracy.
In a 2015 PLOS One study from the University of Iowa and UC Davis, pigeons were rewarded with food for correct answers. A flock of four, voting together, reached 99 percent. The researchers say pigeons could help test imaging tools, not replace doctors.
Could you beat a pigeon?
first_comment: The birds struggled with the trickiest breast masses, just like people do. Would you trust a pigeon to double check your homework?
